Definition: from G5228 and G2192; to hold oneself above, i.e. (figuratively) to excel; participle (as adjective, or neuter as noun) superior, superiority:--better, excellency, higher, pass, supreme.
BiblicalUsage: Scripture uses hyperéchō where we would say to hold above, to excel, to be supreme. In Philippians 2:3, the text says "but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves." In Philippians 3:8, the text says "and I count all things [but] loss for the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord."
TheologicalSignificance: I take hyperéchō to mean that authority belongs to God first; every other authority answers to His. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
